prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE exceptionally polished desktop website design comp, 1536x1024 landscape: a real web layout, edge to edge, no device frame, no browser chrome.

The FIRST attached image is the approved look and feel for this page: match its header, type, spacing, white cards, canary-yellow buttons and highlights, and above all its premium matte isometric miniature desk (pale wood desktop, green blotter, a small canary, an open brass birdcage, soft studio daylight, one contact shadow). The other attached images are the same site's built homepage: they confirm the header (script wordmark "Birdcar" at left; nav "How I work", "Selected work", "Writing" and a canary-yellow pill "Book a free Walkthrough →"), the pale daylight ground #edf3f0, near-black ink #0b141a, the heavy tight grotesk (Mona Sans) for all text, white pill tags, and canary yellow #f7c848 only on actions and highlights. Do NOT copy any reference's content beyond that style; do not paint invented words on props (no text on notebooks, book spines, or signs).

This page is "The Walkthrough": the booking page for a free, pitch-free, roughly one-hour conversation with Nick (Birdcar), a systems engineer who builds tools for established service businesses. Within three business days the visitor gets a written report they keep: what's happening, what I recommend, and where I'd start. New requirement for this page: the visitor qualifies themselves before reaching the calendar. The fit check uses these exact lines: "You have customers and people doing the work." / "One process takes too much chasing, copying, or remembering." / "I can talk to the people who do it." and the honest disqualifier "If I can't talk to the people doing the work, I'm not the right fit."

STRUCTURE, in reading order (the questions lead to the desk: qualification first, the calendar waits at the end of the page):
1. Header, about 80px, as the reference.
2. First viewport, two columns. LEFT (x 80 to 690): headline about 64px, two lines: "An hour on the work. A report you can use." Paragraph at about 19px: "In a free Walkthrough, you spend about an hour showing me the work that's giving you trouble. Within three business days you get my recommendations in writing." One medium line: "The hour is about your work. If you want to talk about hiring me, you'll bring it up, not me." A canary-yellow button "Check the fit, then pick a time ↓" and a muted line "About an hour. A written report within three business days. Free."
RIGHT (x 740 to 1460, y 100 to 700): the miniature desk from the reference, but the object on it is the report, not the calendar: a white report card standing on the desk titled "Your Walkthrough report" with three rows "What's happening", "What I recommend", "Where I'd start" (canary-yellow row). The canary perches on the report card's top corner; the open brass birdcage sits at the desk's right end.
3. Lower band (y 740 to 1024) on white, the start of the qualification section, set as a large question on the left and three check rows on the right: left heading about 44px "Is this a fit?"; right, three rows separated by hairlines, each with a round ink-outlined check circle and the line at about 22px: "You have customers and people doing the work." "One process takes too much chasing, copying, or remembering." "I can talk to the people who do it." Under them, a muted line: "If I can't talk to the people doing the work, I'm not the right fit."

ART DIRECTION: one dominant move, the desk with the report; the fit check below is calm, large, and legible. Premium, adult, precise. Not cute. No purple, no gradient orbs, no robots, no AI imagery, no stock photos, no prices, no fake metrics, no testimonials. Preserve all quoted words exactly. Treat it as a finished, shippable website.
